gap: No result ChatGPT got states that MC4 is a Stäubli connector family whose maker says Original MC4 and MC4-EVO 2 must never be mated with other makers' 'MC4-compatible' connectors. Mismatched pairs can 'cause cracks, leakage, and increased contact resistance … at worst … a fire'. The 2020 NEC 690.33(C) allows non-identical connectors only if they are 'listed and identified for intermatability'. So a premium genuine-Stäubli extension does not guarantee an approved connection on a portable panel whose maker names no MC4 brand.
standout_why: I compared against both cited pages (yourpowersetup.com, stormwatts.com compatibility) and the top uncited ones (ridgewatt.com, powerstationtips.com, stormwatts brand-vs-third-party, backup-power.org). They cover connector-to-port matching, XT60 vs XT60i, polarity, voltage drop by wire gauge, and cold-weather Voc. I checked each fetched page for cross-mating, Stäubli, UL 6703 and NEC 690.33, and none mentions any of them. ChatGPT's #1 pick was described as 'Genuine Stäubli MC4 connectors' and presented as the quality choice, with no warning about mating it with a panel's own connectors.
decides: This changes the pick. For the run from a portable panel to the station, the cable to buy is the panel or station maker's own extension and adapter, because those are sold as matched to that maker's panels. For BLUETTI SORA panels that is the BLUETTI Solar Extension Cable (30 A, MC4 male + female, $59) plus the BLUETTI 20 A MC4-to-XT60 cable ($29). A genuine-Stäubli 10 AWG extension is the right pick only when the panel's own leads are genuine Stäubli MC4. Otherwise Stäubli's own instructions rule out that mating, so the higher price buys no certainty at the panel joint.

findings.label: Connector maker's position on cross-mating MC4 with other makers' connectors
findings.value: "Cross-mating of connectors can cause cracks, leakage, and increased contact resistance of the connection system… often results in connector failures, power loss, and safety hazards. At worst, this damage may even lead to a fire."
findings.source_title: Avoid Cross-mating of PV Connectors (Stäubli Electrical Connectors, Inc., AltEnergyMag, 2022-04-21)
findings.note: Stäubli, the company that makes MC4, wrote this article. It cites IEC 60364-7-712:2017: 'male and female connectors […] shall be of the same type from the same manufacturer'. It also cites IEC 62852 and UL 6703. It gives no contact-resistance or temperature figures.

findings.label: US code rule for mating PV connectors of different brands
findings.value: 2020 NEC 690.33(C): "Where mating connectors are not of the identical type and brand, they shall be listed and identified for intermatability", used "as described in the manufacturer's instructions"
findings.source_title: Mismatched Connectors Are a Common Cause of Safety and Reliability Issues in Solar Installations (Advanced Energy, Colin Thompson, 2023-11-01)
findings.note: This is a secondary quote of the NEC text, because the NFPA text sits behind a login. Advanced Energy names the mechanism: 'slight differences in dimensions and materials can cause resistance, leading to heat buildup and eventual failed connections', and mismatched pairs 'may work at first'. NEC rules apply to installations. A portable panel on the ground is a use case that rule does not clearly reach, so present this as a safety rule, not a legal requirement for campers.
